note: Researched 2026-09-03 as part of a _famous-germany.json batch verification pass. All three trees verify against the two-source bar and have confirmed tree-level coordinates, but only three candidates exist and none individually clears the 2026-08-31 single-tree-destination exception (a good regional monumental tree, not a would-travel-for-this-one destination). Below the 4-tree floor, so held here rather than published. A future pass should look for a fourth Giessen tree (city itself, Schiffenberg monastery grounds, botanical garden) to complete the cluster; Adam und Eva sits 5.4km from the Roedgen pair (Alte Eiche + Schillerlinde, which are ~410m apart and walkable together), so a real Giessen page would be two stops rather than one.

leads.name: Adam und Eva (Wieseck)
leads.species_basis: Two independent sources (Giessen's own Naturdenkmal register via German Wikipedia; monumentale-eichen.de / baumkunde.de) both call these Trauben-Eiche (sessile oak), not Quercus robur despite the genus-only lead entry saying Oak (Quercus sp.)
leads.girth_cm: conflicting: official Giessen Naturdenkmal register (via de.wikipedia Liste der Naturdenkmaeler in Giessen) gives approx. 420cm and 520cm for the two trees, heights approx. 25m and 30m; monumentale-eichen.de and baumkunde.de (2020 measurement) give 442cm and 595cm, height 33m for the pair. Both describe a monumental, unbranched trunk over 10m on the larger tree.
leads.verify_notes: Twin sessile oaks in the Badenburger Wald, officially designated Naturdenkmal and (per baumkunde) also a Baumveteran-registered pair; documented in Hans Joachim Froehlich's 1990 book on historic trees. Genuinely old and one has a striking >10m unbranched monumental trunk, but this is a solid regional monumental-tree pair rather than a singular famous destination, so it does not clear the single-tree exception on its own. Access: public forest, Badenburger Wald, no restriction found. GOOD CANDIDATE if a 4th Giessen tree turns up.
leads.access: Free, public forest (Badenburger Wald); no access restriction found.

leads.name: Alte Eiche (Rödgen)

location.address: Corner of Geiselweg/Seeweg, Rödgen, Giessen, on a former forest picnic clearing

leads.verify_notes: Under state protection since 3 September 1906 (one of the oldest protection dates found in this batch), per monumentale-eichen.de. Official Giessen Naturdenkmal register gives ca. 275-300 years, 16m tall, 610cm girth; monumentale-eichen.de gives ca. 350 years, 15m, 629cm girth (measured 2018). Trunk shows real decline: a triangular opening sealed with grating on one side, bark missing on the other, a horizontal branch propped on two steel tubes. Still described as vital overall. Roughly 410m from the Schillerlinde, walkable together. GOOD CANDIDATE if a 4th Giessen tree turns up.
leads.access: Free, public clearing off Seeweg; no restriction found.

leads.name: Schillerlinde (Rödgen)

location.address: Geiselstrauchkopf, edge of Rödgen, Giessen, near the sports field

leads.verify_notes: Planted 11 November 1859 for the 100th birthday of Friedrich von Schiller, one of hundreds planted across 400-500 German towns in that Schiller year; officially a Naturdenkmal. This is the rare case in the batch with a genuinely documented planting date, so age is exact rather than estimated (167 years as of 2026). Modest size for its age (197cm girth), a memorial tree rather than a giant. A local SPD-Roedgen page (spd-roedgen.de) reportedly connects it to a historical protest against local nobility during the village's Grenzgang tradition, but that page 403'd on this pass and was not independently confirmed; worth another attempt. GOOD CANDIDATE if a 4th Giessen tree turns up; only ~410m from Alte Eiche.
leads.access: Free, on municipal ground near the sports field; no restriction found.
